name: Sliced pineapple

steps.action: Cut off the top and base so the pineapple stands flat.
steps.cue: It sits steady on the board.
steps.why: A flat base makes it safe to cut.

steps.action: Slice the skin off downward in strips, following the curve.
steps.why: Following the curve wastes less fruit.
steps.watch_out: Dig out any remaining brown eyes.

steps.action: Cut into rings or chunks, removing the hard core in the middle. Chill if you have time.
steps.cue: No woody core in the pieces.
steps.why: The core is tough and fibrous.

doneness_signature: Bright, juicy pineapple pieces with no skin or core.

rescue.fix: A tiny pinch of salt over the pieces tames the acidity and lifts the sweetness.

level_up.how: Dust with a little chilli and squeeze lime over for a street-style treat.

name: Watermelon slices

steps.action: Cut the watermelon in half, then into wedges.
steps.why: Wedges are easy to handle and serve.

steps.action: Slice the flesh off the rind, or serve as wedges to bite. Cut into cubes for a bowl. Best cold.
steps.cue: Juicy red flesh, white rind left behind.
steps.why: The simplest way to end a meal light.

doneness_signature: Cold, crisp watermelon, cubed or in wedges.

rescue.fix: Chill well and add a squeeze of lime.

level_up.how: Scatter crumbled feta and torn mint over the cubes.

name: Fruit salad

difficulty.label: Easy
drivers: Only care is keeping soft fruit from browning

ingredients.item: Mixed fruit (pineapple, watermelon, pawpaw, banana, apple)

steps.action: Wash and peel the fruits that need it.
Cut everything into similar bite-sized cubes so it mixes evenly.
steps.why: Uniform pieces mix and eat better.

steps.action: Add banana and apple last and stir gently. Add a spoon of milk or yogurt if you like it creamy. Chill and serve.
steps.why: Banana and apple brown and mush if mixed too early or too hard.
steps.watch_out: A squeeze of lime keeps apple and banana from browning.

doneness_signature: A bright, fresh bowl of evenly cut fruit, lightly creamy if you like.

rescue.fix: Toss with lime juice and serve soon; add fresh-cut fruit on top.

level_up.how: Layer with yogurt and a scatter of groundnut or granola in a glass.

name: Puff puff

difficulty.label: Intermediate
drivers: The yeast rise can't be rushed and needs warmth
Frying at the right temperature so they cook through without burning

time.overlap_note: The 45-60 minute rise is hands-off but unskippable — plan for it.
make_ahead: Mix the batter and let it rise

steps.action: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, salt and nutmeg. Add warm water slowly, stirring to a thick, stretchy batter (between cake batter and dough).
steps.cue: Thick batter that falls in a stretchy ribbon off the spoon.
steps.why: Too runny and it won't hold a ball; too stiff and it won't puff.
steps.watch_out: Use WARM, not hot, water — hot water kills the yeast.

steps.action: Cover and leave in a warm spot until it doubles and looks bubbly, 45-60 minutes. Don't rush it.
steps.cue: Doubled in size, surface covered in bubbles.
steps.why: This rise is the entire reason puff puff is fluffy. The old recipe buried it in the steps without counting the time.
steps.watch_out: A cold room slows the rise — find somewhere warm.

steps.action: Heat a deep pot of oil on medium. Test with a small drop — it should float up and brown gently, not burn fast.
steps.cue: A test drop rises and sizzles steadily.
steps.why: Deep, medium-hot oil lets the balls cook through to the centre.
steps.watch_out: Too hot = raw inside, burnt outside.

steps.action: Scoop small balls of batter by hand or spoon into the oil. Fry, turning, 3-4 minutes until golden brown all over. Drain.
steps.cue: Round, deep golden, cooked to the centre.
steps.why: Turning gives an even round shape and colour.
steps.watch_out: Fry in batches so the oil stays hot.

doneness_signature: Round, golden, fluffy puff puff, soft and airy inside.

rescue.fix: Yeast was dead or the rise too short. Give the batter more warm-spot time; check the yeast is in date.
Lower the oil heat and fry a little longer so the centre cooks.

level_up.how: Toss warm in cinnamon-sugar, or drizzle with a chocolate or caramel glaze.

name: Chin chin

difficulty.label: Intermediate
drivers: Making and rolling a firm dough by feel
Cutting evenly so pieces fry at the same rate
Frying low and slow so they crisp without burning

time.overlap_note: Cut all the dough before you start frying.

steps.action: Mix the flour, sugar, salt and nutmeg. Rub in the butter with your fingers until it looks like breadcrumbs.
steps.why: Rubbing in the butter makes the chin chin crisp and short.

steps.action: Add the egg and a little milk, and mix to a firm, smooth dough. Don't make it sticky.
steps.cue: Firm dough that holds together and isn't tacky.
steps.why: Firm dough cuts cleanly and fries crunchy.
steps.watch_out: Add liquid sparingly — sticky dough is hard to cut.

steps.action: Roll the dough flat and cut into small squares or strips.
steps.why: Even pieces fry at the same rate.
steps.watch_out: Thin = crunchy; thick = chewy. Pick your style and stay consistent.

steps.action: Heat oil on medium and fry the pieces, stirring, 4-5 minutes until golden. Drain and cool.
steps.cue: Golden and they crisp further as they cool.
steps.why: Low-and-slow frying dries them to a crunch without burning.
steps.watch_out: Don't crowd the pot; stir so they brown evenly.

doneness_signature: Golden, crunchy little bites that keep for days in a sealed jar.

rescue.fix: Fry longer on lower heat to dry them out; they crisp as they cool.
Lower the heat — they need time, not high heat.

level_up.how: Work desiccated coconut into the dough, or add a little orange zest.

name: Banana & groundnut

steps.action: Peel the bananas.
Eat alternating bites of banana and groundnut, or slice the banana into a bowl and scatter groundnut over.
steps.why: The classic Nigerian roadside pairing — no cooking.

doneness_signature: Sweet banana with crunchy, salty groundnut.

rescue.fix: Mash with the groundnut into a quick spread on bread.

level_up.how: Slice the banana, scatter groundnut, drizzle honey and a pinch of cinnamon.

name: Dodo (sweet fried plantain)

difficulty.label: Easy
drivers: Only care is not burning the sugar in very ripe plantain

ingredients.prep: Peeled and cut into cubes or diagonal slices.

steps.action: Peel and cut the plantains into cubes or diagonal slices. The riper they are, the sweeter.
steps.why: Riper plantain caramelises more.

steps.action: Sprinkle lightly with salt to balance the sweetness.
steps.why: Salt makes the sweetness pop.

steps.action: Heat oil on medium and fry 2-3 minutes each side until deep golden and caramelised at the edges. Drain.
steps.cue: Deep golden, caramelised edges, soft centre.
steps.why: Medium heat caramelises without scorching the natural sugars.
steps.watch_out: Very ripe plantain burns fast — watch it closely.

doneness_signature: Deep golden, caramelised, sweet-soft fried plantain.

rescue.fix: Lower the heat; ripe plantain needs gentler frying.

level_up.how: Dust warm with cinnamon-sugar, or serve with a scoop of ice cream.

name: Zobo drink
surprise_note: Most people buy zobo leaves to make tea-like drinks plain. Steeping it with pineapple skin and ginger makes a far better homemade chilled drink to close a meal.

difficulty.label: Simple
drivers: Only judgement is the sweetness and steep time

time.overlap_note: The boil and steep are hands-off; then it needs chilling time too.
make_ahead: Boil and chill ahead of serving

steps.action: Boil the zobo leaves with the pineapple skins, ginger and cloves in plenty of water for 20 minutes.
steps.why: Boiling extracts the colour and flavour from the dried petals.
steps.watch_out: Use plenty of water — it reduces as it boils.

steps.action: Turn off the heat and let it steep another 10 minutes.
steps.why: Steeping pulls out more flavour without boiling it bitter.

steps.action: Strain out the leaves and solids.
Sweeten to taste while still warm so the sugar dissolves, then cool and chill.
steps.why: Sugar dissolves better in warm liquid.
steps.watch_out: Serve cold — it's a chilled drink.

doneness_signature: A deep ruby-red, sweet-tart, ginger-bright chilled drink.

rescue.fix: Add more sugar or pineapple juice.
Boil with more leaves and steep longer.

level_up.how: Add cinnamon stick, a splash of pineapple and orange juice, and serve over ice with mint.
